analysis.title: S&P 500 Futures: What Stops the Selling?
key_insights: Non-Dealer S&P 500 futures selling continued through September 29th per the Commitment of Traders. Non-Dealers sold $10.5bn from September 22nd to 29th, the 5th week of selling in the past 6 since August 18th, for a net -$63.7bn.
Shorts dominated the latest release, though long unwinds accounted for more than 70% of selling across the 1.5 month window.
Asset Managers led the selling, at $11.7bn in the latest report, with Other selling $1.1bn. Hedge Funds bought $620mm and Non-Reportable bought $1.6bn.

Asset Manager liquidation of $5.5bn coincided with a 25bp jump in US 10 year real yields. The rolling 3 month correlation between Asset Manager gross longs and USGGT10Y moved well into negative territory. Proximity to quarter-end suggests asset reallocation may have started early.

Lower probabilities of an imminent Fed hike boosted equities. Below-consensus PCE, dovish Fed speakers and a Nonfarm payrolls miss reduced October hike pricing, enabling a 0.70% recovery in the S&P index.
S&P futures flows arguably remained bearish because deferred real rates rose marginally. The December Adjusted Interest Rate future, a funding proxy, cheapened by about 5bps.
Asset Manager net length stood at a 77% 2 year rank on September 29th, before additional probable sales. GS expects ongoing challenges for S&P futures until yields convincingly reverse.
GS rates research sees recent developments and valuation as a clearer skew toward lower yields, despite upward pressure from oil and resilient AI investment plans.
